title: Kerma, the kingdom Egyptians called Kush
summary: The city-state of Kerma controlled the Nile Valley between the first and fourth cataracts, an area as large as Egypt; Egyptians called it Kush.
why: One of Africa's earliest powerful states south of Egypt, a rival and trade partner of the pharaohs.

notes.problem: Source does not call Kerma the 'first great kingdom of Kush'; it says Kerma 'emerged as the dominant political force' and Egyptians identified it as Kush.
